accident_report: V1 (Vehicle A) is traveling eastbound in Lane 1 (rightmost lane for eastbound), a vehicle V2 is traveling in Lane 1, 30 meters behind V1. V2 (Vehicle B) is traveling eastbound in Lane 1, 30 meters behind V1. V3 (Vehicle C) is traveling westbound in Lane 5, which changes into Lane 4 and then merges into the center turn lane. V4 (Vehicle D) is a large bus traveling eastbound in Lane 2, parallel to V1 until it makes a turn. V1 travels in Lane 1 eastbound with V2 following 30 meters behind in the same lane. A line of cars traveling eastbound in Lane 2 includes V4 (a large bus), traveling parallel to V1 until a point where the bus makes a right turn onto a perpendicular street. V3 travels westbound in Lane 5, makes a lane change to Lane 4 to get closer to the center turn lane (Lane 3) where it stops until V4 makes a right turn. With V4 out of sight, V3 makes a left turn across the eastbound lanes (Lanes 1 and 2). However, V1 is still traveling in Lane 1 without the bus V4 obstructing part of the visibility anymore. V1 collides with V3 while V3 makes a left turn which results in a "T-bone" collision where V1 collides directly into the side of V3 because V1 does not have enough time to stop or swerve. V2 might strike the rear of V1 if V1 stops suddenly or swerves to avoid the collision altogether.
